newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Calendar spread closed in BT.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Calendar spread closed in BT.

text.p: UK traded options were relatively quiet as traders drew breath after this week's wild ride in the market, dealers said.

The biggest trade in British Telecommunications was from trader closing calendar spread which was losing money. the deal was to sell 2,000 August 460 calls at 36p and to buy back 2,000 February 460 calls at 44p for a net debit of 8p.
Dealers believed the original position was made for a net credit of 6p.
By 1515 GMT, BT shares were up 19p to 498-1/2p.
Call options in music company EMI Group were busy and the biggest deal was to buy 400 September 1400 calls at 9p possibly on the hope the company will be a takeover target.

And in insurer Royal & Sun Alliance there was a seller of 400 January 500 puts and calls at 52p and 25p each in a short straddle strategy which will make a maximum of 77p profit at expiry if the underlying shares are then 500p.
Over in index options turnover was reduced as traders lacked the incentive to enter the market ahead of the weekend.

"Market volatility has been steady today and we've seen very little retail (institutional) trade," said one dealer who estimated July at-the-money volatility had reduced to 18.5 percent from 24 percent on Thursday.
The biggest deal was to buy 500 September 4625 puts at 66p which was hedged by buying September FTSE futures at 4835 in a volatility trade.
At 1515 GMT cash FTSE was down 23.4 at 4808.3 while September futures were 53 points lower at 4823.
